text:
clair-bot: [vuln-scan] Critical: transitive CVE found in image `redwood/apps/payment:sha8a3` - package=netlib-crypto@2.1.4 CVE-2026-1452
maya: fyi, scanner flagged this during the nightly image-scan.
sam: seeing the same. which layer?
clair-bot: vulnerability located in layer 5 (python deps). SBOM included in artifact metadata.
jamie: can we stop any rollout that uses this image?
deploy-bot: Blocked deployment pipeline `payment-service/*` at sha8a3 per policy:high-severity-vuln.
leila: good call. i'm triaging now — initial ask: do we have any creds baked in or any signed artifacts from this image?
eli: quick check: no AWS keys in layers but there is a leftover `.netrc` entry in a vendor package config (non-prod token).
maya: non-prod token still bad, rotate IG immediately. Also need to regen SBOM and rebuild base if transitive dep can't be patched.
sam: attaching snippet of scan output:```
- package: netlib-crypto
  version: 2.1.4
  cves:
    - CVE-2026-1452
  path: /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/vendor/netlib-crypto
  fix: Upgrade to >=2.2.0
```
leila: thanks. creating GH issue and PR template: https://github.com/redwoodinc/payment-service/issues/new?template=sec-vuln.md -> will link PR after bump.
jamie: i'll open a Jira ticket SEC-312 and add incident type supply-chain. tagging infra oncall.
eli: mitigations: 1) block image (done), 2) rotate any tokens referenced, 3) rebuild with patched dependency + regenerate SBOM, 4) update KMS access audit to check for any recent usage from that image's service account.
maya: do we need emergency KMS rotation? the token found was non-prod but linked to CI runner that has encrypted secrets in KMS. Recommend rotating the non-prod token and auditing KMS decrypt events for the runner key id `key-rc-9a`.
leila: i'll kick rotation for token & open a KMS audit query. can someone run:```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=key-rc-9a --start-time 2026-03-01 --end-time 2026-03-31
```
sam: running now, posting results in thread when ready.
clair-bot: SBOM snapshot (trim):```
- name: payment-service
  version: 1.4.2
  components:
    - name: netlib-crypto
      version: 2.1.4
      evidence: transitive_requirements.txt
```
jamie: timeline note: if rebuild + PR can land within 2 hours, we can unfreeze deployments. otherwise escalate to incident call.
leila: PR created -> https://github.com/redwoodinc/payment-service/pull/428 (bump netlib-crypto to 2.2.1, regen SBOM). Requesting review from @maya and @eli.
eli: reviewing now. if tests pass, we push rebuilt image to staging and run full image-scan again.
maya: also add a postmortem checklist item: ensure vendor config doesn't package tokens; add linter step to CI to strip `.netrc` and similar files before image build.
jamie: agreed. i'll add to SEC-312 remediation tasks and owner assignment.
sam: cloudtrail results: no decrypt events from key-rc-9a tied to this runner in last 30 days. looks limited.
leila: that's good. still rotating the token and updating CI to use short-lived creds.
clair-bot: label `supply-chain:detected` applied and notifier pinged #security-pager.
deploy-bot: pipeline unblocked for non-affected images. blocked image remains `sha8a3`.
eli: after PR merges, let's run a canary deploy to a sandbox and monitor for errors. schedule a 30m validation window.
maya: thanks all — keep updates here. post-incident please attach rebuilt SBOM and link to the deploy logs and the SEC ticket. :thumbsup:
